name: storm-deepresearch-skill
title: STORM DeepResearch Library
job_to_be_done: Transform a research topic, question, URL set, or document pack into an auditable multi-perspective research package whose factual claims are traceable to retrieved evidence and whose Markdown, HTML, and PDF outputs remain content-consistent.

trigger_surface.description: Use for source-grounded deep research that needs multi-perspective question generation, explicit claim-evidence traceability, contradiction and uncertainty handling, and validated Markdown, HTML, and PDF deliverables. Do not use for quick lookup, unsupported role-play, or requests that only need a short answer.
should_trigger: Research a complex topic and produce a cited report with Markdown, HTML, PDF, and an evidence audit.
Use supplied papers and URLs as the starting corpus, retrieve missing evidence, and show contradictions and uncertainty.
Compare competing technical, policy, market, or academic claims and explain what evidence would change the conclusion.
Create an investment, strategy, or decision memo where every material factual claim must be source-traceable.
Perform a literature or industry review with current-source requirements and explicit limitations.
should_not_trigger: Answer one simple factual question that can be resolved with one authoritative source.
Brainstorm fictional expert opinions without retrieval or evidence requirements.
Rewrite, translate, summarize, or format supplied text without doing new research.
Provide legal, medical, or financial advice as a substitute for a qualified professional.
Generate a report where the user explicitly forbids source verification but still asks for factual certainty.
edge_cases: For high-stakes domains, produce an evidence review and limitations, not personalized professional advice.
For user-supplied closed corpora, do not add external sources unless the brief permits them.
When PDF tooling is unavailable, fail the full-package gate unless the user explicitly requested a reduced package.
When evidence is insufficient, return a bounded partial result with unresolved claims instead of completing by inference.
When a topic is time-sensitive, enforce retrieval dates and freshness thresholds from the brief.

steps: Normalize the user request into a validated brief and record assumptions that materially affect scope.
Generate domain-adapted perspective questions; treat perspectives as query generators, never as evidence.
Create a research plan with source priorities, freshness rules, stopping conditions, and retrieval budget.
Retrieve through the host-agent adapter by default or an explicitly configured provider adapter when approved.
Normalize every retrieved item into the source register with provenance, dates, source type, and reliability notes.
Atomize material report claims and link each factual claim to supporting or contradicting source evidence.
Synthesize contradictions, uncertainty, and confidence without forcing unsupported consensus.
Draft report.md as the canonical public report while keeping internal claim and source IDs in audit artifacts.
Run peer review, claim closure, freshness, citation entailment, and leakage checks; revise until gates pass or the run stops as bounded partial.
Render HTML and PDF from report.md, then validate file presence, cross-format consistency, and non-zero failure semantics.
decision_points: Ask one clarification only when the missing answer would materially change scope, source policy, risk, or deliverables.
Choose closed-corpus, host-agent retrieval, or configured provider retrieval from the brief and runtime capabilities.
Require two independent sources for high-impact contested claims when feasible; otherwise lower confidence and preserve the gap.
Stop retrieval when coverage and marginal-value thresholds are met, or when budget or availability limits are reached.
Fail full-package validation when PDF is required but absent; permit a reduced package only when the brief explicitly allows it.
Remove, weaken, or mark unknown any claim that cannot satisfy its evidence policy.
failure_modes: Perspective prose is mistaken for evidence.
A citation exists but does not entail the attached claim.
Source IDs are referenced but absent from the register, or registered sources are never used.
Current claims rely on stale sources without an explicit historical scope.
Contradictory evidence is omitted or silently averaged into false consensus.
Inference and recommendation are presented as facts.
Markdown, HTML, and PDF diverge or contain unresolved template markers.
Validation reports errors but exits successfully.
Public outputs leak local paths, credentials, internal scratch IDs, or debugging metadata.
Retrieval stops without recording the reason and residual coverage gap.
